clauses.statement: When the server cannot resume an offered session and the client supplies a usable full-handshake offer, the server may proceed with a full handshake under a different session ID. A server may also return an empty ID for an uncached new session. Preserve the actual ClientHello in the Finished transcript.

evidence.scope: Legacy full-handshake fallback for WinWAP offers with short or eight-byte stale IDs, tested with captured ClientHello-derived fixtures. Live XP verification of a stale-ID offer and an abbreviated wire handshake are separate milestones.

clauses.statement: A critical connection_close_notify ends the current connection. Session closure also invalidates the session ID. On a later ClientHello the server selects a distinct ID for a new full handshake when it cannot resume the offered session.

evidence.scope: The opt-in probe sends a protected connection close and starts a fresh peer. The buffered XP run completed full handshakes and protected WSP replies before and after the close.
evidence.peerObservation: WinWAP 4.2.0.290 sent empty IDs on every captured ClientHello. WTLS-201 stale-ID fallback remains covered by Rust fixtures. Two direct trials showed a separate clear-alert retry failure. The buffered trial completed both protected exchanges.

clauses.statement: A ClientHello announces the ordered key exchanges and an optional existing session ID. A matching ServerHello ID and abbreviated Finished flight provide observable evidence of session reuse. Authenticated suite offers and a completed certificate-authenticated exchange are distinct evidence.

evidence.scope: Ruflo reviewed the candidate screen. The maintainer ran RIM's stock BlackBerry 7290 simulator in isolated XP and decoded its captured full-handshake offers. The authenticated lab endpoint reported UnsupportedProfile before any ServerHello.
evidence.peerObservation: BlackBerry offered authenticated RSA and 3DES-CBC-EDE with full SHA. The three distinct ClientHellos all had empty IDs. Certificate verification, protected application traffic, and live resumption remain open.

clauses.statement: A full-handshake ServerHello identifies a selected offered key by its one-based index, chooses offered algorithms, and uses a key-refresh value no greater than the client's. The Finished calculation covers the actual handshake messages. A full exchange on cache miss selects a different session ID.

evidence.scope: Authenticated suite selection and exact transcript with live BlackBerry full handshakes, protected WSP traffic and cache-miss fallback. Ruflo verified the exact candidate and 57 locked offline Cargo tests passed.
evidence.peerObservation: Operator compared the displayed leaf thumbprint and accepted the lab certificate at the stock trust prompt for each full handshake. BlackBerry reoffered ac51a992d73be1a9 after protected connection closure. The server sent 7877de87c4ade752 and completed a second full handshake. Automatic CA trust and wire resumption remain open.

clauses.statement: A matched session ID allows a server-first abbreviated Finished exchange under the cached master secret. Fresh hello randoms produce connection-local keys and current record epochs. Protected connection close preserves a cacheable session while protected session close invalidates it.

evidence.scope: Authenticated cache and abbreviated wire exchange, verified with deterministic native peers. WTLS-206 tracks the BlackBerry key-index observation.

clauses.statement: An abbreviated ServerHello may use zero for the ignored key field. If there is a matching offered key exchange, the server can return its one-based index. The echoed session ID and server-first Finished flight still identify resumption.

evidence.scope: Native tests verify the resumed index with full and abbreviated-only offers. The reviewed code also resumed a real cached BlackBerry connection after a protected connection close.
evidence.peerObservation: Both reconnect hellos carried a3ae109830b84aa6. The server committed first, verified the client Finished and received the acknowledgement for its protected WSP reply.

clauses.statement: A verified fatal alert terminates the connection and invalidates its session. A verified critical alert terminates the connection and may preserve the session. Connection close preserves the session, session close invalidates it, and a clear observation has no authority to invalidate an existing valid session.

evidence.scope: Exact Ruflo review and 82 deterministic Rust tests. Native peers tested generic alerts in committed and provisional receive epochs. The stock BlackBerry exercised protected Connection and Session close and verified post-close WSP traffic.
evidence.peerObservation: Connection close preserved 7ae7417145b8ac4b. After Session close, the handset offered 7ae7417145b8ac4b and the server performed a full handshake with beba37cb32ed50c1.

clauses.statement: A datagram transport preserves association routing and service data unit boundaries, and drives the protocol retry timer after lost delivery. With one server session context, Connection close allows an abbreviated reconnect and Session close causes a full reconnect when the peer offers its prior ID.

evidence.scope: Exact Ruflo review and 91 Rust tests. Dropping a server flight in the deterministic adapter link preserved the original retransmission bytes and allowed a protected echo. A real loopback socket exercised whole datagram delivery. A separate live run exercised both close scopes on the checked-in sample.
evidence.peerObservation: BlackBerry resumed 9db23b7437c71aed after Connection close and reoffered it after Session close. The sample issued 1ec65ed3a1559f86 in a full handshake. Matching protected WSP page acknowledgments followed all three handshakes.

clauses.statement: For the implemented authenticated datagram profile, select the protected record key block using the record's explicit sequence number. Ordinary loss or in-window out-of-order arrival across a key refresh allows later valid delivery. A repeated record is delivered at most once.

evidence.scope: Exact Ruflo review and 93 Rust tests. The deterministic adapter tests use locally generated authenticated traffic to verify delivery across a refresh boundary under loss, duplication and reordering. Application retransmission remains an upper-layer responsibility. The existing production path passed these cases without a protocol change.

clauses.statement: In the opt-in authenticated profile, a gateway certificate is verified against its provisioned issuing authority and selected against the offered authority list. The RSA authority identifier hashes raw unsigned modulus bytes. The client verifies the native leaf independently. Cache resumption preserves the approved same-trust-context and conflicting-list rules.

evidence.scope: Exact Ruflo review and 99 Rust tests. Deterministic evidence covers the explicitly selected provisioned profile, RSA authority ID encoding, matching/empty/nonmatching offers, independent leaf validation, and resumption, including conflicting offers and cache-context changes.
evidence.peerObservation: The live provisioned BlackBerry check remains a separate milestone.

clauses.source: WAP-199 §§10.5.1.2 and 10.5.2 with WAP-199_104/_105 §3.3 and OMA WSP content type 0x18
clauses.statement: After native CA enrollment the stock BlackBerry advertises the lab issuing authority and authenticates the WTLS-210 gateway leaf during a full handshake.

evidence.scope: Ruflo historical source review, filtered before-and-after capture, and matching protected WSP acknowledgment. CA trust was explicitly granted during enrollment. No leaf exception was used. Same simulator run.

clauses.source: Live BlackBerry 7290 restart observation, with WAP-199 §§10.5.1.2 and 10.5.2
clauses.statement: The stock BlackBerry 7290 simulator retains the enrolled lab authority across a graceful process restart on the same XP overlay. It authenticates a newly keyed gateway leaf signed by that authority without a certificate prompt.

evidence.scope: Ruflo plan review, confirmed Windows process exit and relaunch, exact CA entry in both ClientHellos, separate gateway leaves and fresh caches, and two full handshakes with verified protected WSP acknowledgments. No re-enrollment or leaf approval after restart.

clauses.statement: With the lab CA enrolled, the stock BlackBerry 7290 authenticates the gateway in a full handshake, resumes after protected Connection close, and performs a new full handshake after protected Session close without certificate prompts.

evidence.peerObservation: The handset reoffered ff638f53df37b626 after both closes. The gateway echoed it after Connection close, and after Session close issued 25ec9d1c3e978698 in a full handshake. Matching protected page acknowledgments were 0fb2, 0161 and 2f75.
evidence.scope: Ruflo plan review and live verification on one isolated stock simulator and one strict gateway process. Native CA enrollment occurred once before the run. Certificate prompts stayed enabled, with no leaf approval. A protected client application record arrived after each close and the gateway discarded it before the next handshake.

clauses.statement: In the provisioned authenticated UDP profile, either endpoint can send sequence 65535 once for a new record. Attempting another new record retires the connection with a typed sequence-exhaustion diagnostic and preserves the eligible session at its original expiry. A distinct verified fatal or explicit/session close still invalidates as applicable.

evidence.scope: Exact Ruflo review and 107 Rust tests. Both provisioned wire roles exercise the last record, automatic retirement, and resumption with the preserved session. Coverage includes alert output, explicit invalidation, and UDP retirement.

clauses.statement: During a full UDP handshake, loss of the final server CCS/Finished SDU triggers byte-identical retransmission of the entire client commit at its deadline and byte-identical retransmission of the server commit in response. The recovered association carries protected application data.

evidence.scope: Exact Ruflo review and 108 Rust tests. The deterministic adapter link dropped only the final server CCS/Finished datagram of a full handshake. It verified the exact client retry deadline, byte-identical client and server SDUs, no duplicate establishment, and protected application echo after recovery.

clauses.statement: The supported Rust client and server encode the exact supplied Unix seconds in the first four bytes of each hello Random on both full and abbreviated handshakes. The independent monotonic millisecond clock drives scheduling and cache timing.

evidence.scope: Exact Ruflo review and 110 Rust tests. The deterministic adapter tests check the first four Random bytes in the emitted ClientHello and ServerHello against the exact supplied Unix seconds in both handshake modes. Each sender has its own wall clock, and each uses a different value on resumption. Independent monotonic milliseconds govern the adapter. The abbreviated exchange echoes a cached ID and completes on both endpoints.

clauses.source: WAP-199-WTLS-20000218-a §10.4 and Appendix B.4, with WAP-199_103 row S-006
clauses.statement: On a pending inbound server association, an exact duplicate of the accepted ClientHello receives its entire cached server flight. An admissible fresh ClientHello can replace the pending handshake in the same slot and retains the original slot deadline, with verified cached sessions and established associations preserved.

evidence.scope: Exact Ruflo review and 114 Rust tests. Deterministic UDP cases verify same-slot full and abbreviated replacement, byte-identical duplicate replies, rejection of retired and conflicting hellos, the original pending deadline, and protected exchange. Rejected candidates and fresh hellos on established tuples preserve the existing peer. Scope is the pending handshake in the standalone adapter.

clauses.statement: An eligible clear alert is correlated by its complete sent-record checksum. A matching fatal or critical error can end a pending clear receive negotiation while preserving verified cached sessions. Clear alerts have no closure or invalidation effect on an authenticated connection.

evidence.scope: Exact Ruflo review and 122 Rust tests. The supported clear receive path correlates alerts to a complete record from the pending attempt. Matched terminal errors retire that attempt, preserve eligible cache entries and honor the no_connection sequence exception. Rejection and advisory cases preserve sequence and retry state. Committed connections retain protected delivery. Outbound certificate alerts remain separate.

clauses.statement: The supported UDP profile accepts multiple independently protected application records per datagram in both roles, including an authenticated abbreviated client commit suffix. It preserves record boundaries, replay admission, close references, and terminal alert precedence.

evidence.scope: Exact Ruflo review and 129 Rust tests. Both UDP roles receive independently protected application records in datagram order, including after an abbreviated client commit. Tests cover both length forms, replay and key refresh, invalid suffix rollback, the UDP budget, verified commit retries, and close checksum and cache effects. Outbound batching and general content-type interleaving remain separate scope. BlackBerry evidence covers single-record traffic.

clauses.statement: The provisioned client returns a typed local certificate rejection and one clear fatal reply for a classified native leaf failure in a complete full server flight. The gateway can retire the pending attempt while eligible verified sessions retain their original expiry.

evidence.workflow: The Ruflo implementation worker was interrupted. The abandoned claim retained the checkpoints. The maintainer ran the packet and full Cargo gates and a separate pinned, read-only Ruflo review against the exact implementation commit.
evidence.scope: Exact Ruflo review and 137 Rust tests. A classified native leaf rejection on the provisioned client's full handshake returns a typed diagnostic and a clear fatal reply. Wire tests cover alert mapping, exact record bytes and checksum, one-shot behavior, and local failures. UDP tests cover delivery, loss, and retirement. A rejected fallback preserves the eligible verified session at its original expiry. The manual and diagnostic-only entry points keep their existing contract.
